blockMcqs.question: What does cache coherence guarantee?
options: Faster clock speeds for all cores
All caches agree on a shared value
Every core has an identical cache size
Memory never runs out of space
blockMcqs.explanation: Coherence keeps every core's cached copy of a location consistent with the others.

blockMcqs.question: Why does Core B see a stale value after Core A writes x?
options: Core B's cache is broken
Core B still holds its old cached copy
Main memory deleted the variable
Core A used a different variable name
blockMcqs.explanation: Without coherence, a write only updates the writer's own cache, leaving other copies stale.

blockMcqs.question: How does coherence differ from consistency?
options: They are the same guarantee
Coherence is per-address; consistency governs cross-address order
Consistency only applies to single-core systems
Coherence governs disk writes only
blockMcqs.explanation: Coherence keeps one location in sync; consistency defines visible ordering across locations.

blockMcqs.question: Why does write-invalidate beat write-update in practice?
options: It sends full data on every write
It sends one small message instead of broadcasting data
It disables caching entirely
It only works with one core
blockMcqs.explanation: Invalidation messages are small; broadcasting updated data on every write wastes bus bandwidth.

blockMcqs.question: What is snooping-based coherence built on?
options: A central directory of sharers
Every cache watching a shared bus
Disk-based logging of writes
Manual software locks only
blockMcqs.explanation: Snooping caches observe bus traffic and invalidate their own copies when they see a conflicting write.

blockMcqs.question: What problem does a directory-based protocol solve?
options: It removes the need for cache lines
It avoids broadcasting to every core on a write
It makes all cores share one cache
It eliminates the need for main memory
blockMcqs.explanation: A directory tracks sharers per line so invalidations go only to cores that hold a copy, avoiding broadcast.

blockMcqs.question: In MESI, what does the Modified state mean?
options: Clean and shared with other caches
Dirty, changed only in this cache
Unusable, must be refetched
Clean and held by no one else
blockMcqs.explanation: Modified means this cache has the only copy and it differs from main memory (dirty).

blockMcqs.question: What must a core do before reading an Invalid line?
options: Nothing, it can read directly
Fetch a fresh copy first
Mark it Modified immediately
Wait for a directory reset
blockMcqs.explanation: Invalid means the copy is unusable, so the core must fetch the current value before reading.

blockMcqs.question: What does the Exclusive state save compared to a 3-state protocol?
options: Disk I/O on every read
A bus message when later writing an unshared line
The need for an Invalid state
Main memory capacity
blockMcqs.explanation: Exclusive marks a line as sole-owned, so a later write can happen silently without checking other caches.

blockMcqs.question: What causes false sharing?
options: Two threads editing the same variable
Two unrelated variables sharing one cache line
A cache line that is too small
Disabling the coherence protocol
blockMcqs.explanation: When unrelated variables land on one line, writes to either invalidate the whole line for other cores.

blockMcqs.question: Is false sharing a correctness bug or a performance bug?
options: Correctness bug, results are wrong
Performance bug only, results stay correct
Both equally
Neither, it doesn't affect real programs
blockMcqs.explanation: False sharing only adds coherence overhead; the program's output remains correct.

blockMcqs.question: How does padding a struct help avoid false sharing?
options: It compresses the data to fit one line
It spaces variables onto separate cache lines
It disables the cache for that struct
It merges variables into a single word
blockMcqs.explanation: Padding pushes each hot variable onto its own cache line so cores stop invalidating each other.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement about coherence is accurate?
options: Coherence guarantees a race-free program
Coherence says nothing about cross-address ordering
Snooping never generates bus traffic
False sharing corrupts program output
blockMcqs.explanation: Coherence only keeps single addresses in sync; ordering across addresses is consistency's job.
